answers: lens-scope-design finding 1:** done — corrected in Round 6; the step area for DSDIFF-1/DSDIFF-2 tests was changed from `plugins/agent/build/tests/` to `tests/unit/, tests/integration/`; the current design-draft.md already reflects this fix at step 3.

lens-scope-design finding 2:** wrong — the issue scope section names test files only for RQDIFF-1/RQDIFF-2/RQDIFF-3; it is entirely silent about where the RQEND-1/DSEND-1 test should go. No existing file is named for that check. A new file in `tests/unit/` is consistent with the step area and repository test layout. The scope lens is treating the issue's file list as an exhaustive constraint on a requirement the list never addresses.

build-tests finding 1:** not mine — this is `lens-security-code finding 1` about a hardcoded commit SHA in the test-author's implementation of DSLOCK-3; the design spec says "git diff is run between the base commit and HEAD" which does not prescribe a hardcoded SHA; the test-author must implement the git diff comparison using a non-hardcoded reference (e.g., `ZBUILD_BASE_SHA` environment variable or `git merge-base`); the finding is about test implementation, not the design spec.

build-tests finding 2:** not mine — this is `lens-red-team-code finding 3`, identical concern to build-tests finding 1; same test file, same hardcoded SHA, same reasoning — the design spec does not require a hardcoded SHA and the test-author must implement without one.

build-tests finding 3:** wrong — this is `lens-correctness-code finding 2`; RQDIFF-3 requires only that "behavior remains as today" for the `done_sentinel` path; DSDIFF-3 is a [done] guard that the two events (build.discrepancy.detected and build.diff.empty_after_done_sentinel) still fire; a `terminated_reason` payload assertion for the done_sentinel case would add test depth beyond what RQDIFF-3 specifies; already answered as lens-correctness-code finding 2 in an earlier round.

build-tests finding 4:** wrong — this is `lens-sre-code finding 2`; scanning all of `route.sh` rather than only `route_to_model_loop`'s body is more conservative, not less accurate; `signal` assigned in `_route_signal_handler` is a value `route_to_model_loop` reaches via its signal handler and belongs in the enumerated set; already answered as lens-sre-code finding 2 in an earlier round.
